correctness.rationale: Exact time-dependent urn transition probabilities yield (n+1)a_(n+1)=n a_n+s_n for the positive killed chain, with a_1=s_1=1. The reflection identity for absorbed symmetric walk bounds its m-step survival by 2x/sqrt(m), and a monotone even-parity uniform coupling dominates the inhomogeneous Friedman walk while positive. Thus s_(2n)<=2n^(-3/2)(1+sum_(k<n)s_k). Starting with s_n=O(n^(-1/2)), three iterations give O(n^(-1)), O((log n)n^(-3/2)) (summability), and finally O(n^(-3/2)). Discrete tail summation yields finite moments theta<3/2; 889 finite checks, including exact rational recurrences and deterministic square-root bound checks confirm transition and moment recursions and reflected kernel. No finite test is presented as proof.

originality.rationale: The 2025 first-public Balaji–Mahmoud paper states the precise E[T]<infinity problem as a simulation-backed conjecture in Section 5; the theorem proves that property and strengthens it with a polynomial tail upper bound. Earlier urn/drift and Eulerian-deviation papers inspected do not prove the killed survival result. Search incompleteness remains an explicit priority risk.
residual_risks: A previously unindexed theorem on path-dependent Eulerian-descent first-passage times might imply the statement after a nontrivial reduction.
Generic hitting-time moment criteria for time-inhomogeneous supermartingales may encompass the model; the reflection/bootstrap proof is nonetheless fully explicit.
A search for published mathematical records does not establish global novelty or independence.

value.rationale: This directly answers a named open finite-first-return expectation question about a classical nonexchangeable urn walk. The additional n^(-3/2) survival estimate and theta<3/2 moment range distinguish strong first-passage information from marginal recurrence. The proof is an interpretable stopped-moment identity plus a nontrivial iterative comparison. No downstream paper-sized contribution or claimed optimal exponent is needed for this concrete natural gap.
